name: SLOVENIA

flag.title: Flag of Slovenia
flag.note: Blue, white & red with Triglav crest

lead: Slovenia is tiny but spectacular: Alpine peaks, turquoise rivers and ancient caves fill a space smaller than Wales. Drive from snowy mountains to an Adriatic beach in under two hours. About 2 million people call it home, speaking Slovenian. The capital Ljubljana nestles beneath a hilltop castle on a winding river.

geo: Slovenia packs four landscapes into one small country. The Julian Alps crown the north-west with jagged peaks, while the Karst plateau hides Postojna Cave — 24 km of underground passages. The Soča River runs an impossible neon-blue through mountain valleys.

More than 58% of Slovenia is forest — one of Europe's highest ratios. It borders Italy, Austria, Hungary and Croatia. Its Adriatic coastline is just 47 km long, yet includes the medieval gem Piran and a busy harbour at Koper.
animals: Slovenia's forests shelter predators that have vanished from most of Europe. Around 1,000 brown bears roam the southern Kočevje forests — one of the continent's densest populations. Eurasian lynx, grey wolves and golden eagles also live here freely.

The Olm is a blind, pale salamander found only in Karst caves; it survives ten years without food and can live over a century. The fat dormouse inspired a folk harvest hunt, and the Carniolan honeybee is prized worldwide for its gentle nature.
culture: Slovenians are passionate beekeepers — the Carniolan bee is a protected symbol, and painted beehive panels (panjske končnice) form a vivid folk art centuries old. Slovenia's beekeeping tradition is on the UNESCO Intangible Heritage list.

Food means hearty mountain fare: žlikrofi dumplings, štruklji pastry and potica — a walnut-spiral cake for every celebration. Ljubljana's old town is car-free and café-lined, ranking among Europe's greenest capitals.
history: Roman roads crossed Slovenia 2,000 years ago — the city of Emona (today's Ljubljana) bustled by 14 AD. After Rome fell, Slavic tribes arrived in the 6th century; the region then spent centuries under Habsburg Austrian rule.

After WWI, Slovenia joined Yugoslavia. Independence came 25 June 1991; a ten-day war followed before Yugoslav forces withdrew. Slovenia joined NATO and the EU in 2004, then adopted the Euro in 2007 — first ex-Yugoslav republic to do so.
wows: Slovenia is the only country whose name contains the word 'love' (Slo-LOVE-nia).
Postojna Cave has its own railway — tiny electric trains have run inside since 1872.
The blind Olm salamander can live over 100 years, one of the longest-lived amphibians known.
Slovenia has more than 14,000 caves — one of Earth's highest cave densities per km².
The Soča River glows vivid turquoise, visible from the hillsides above.
Ljubljana's entire historic core went car-free in 2007 — locals walk or cycle inside.
Slovenia gave the UN World Bee Day — 20 May, birthday of Anton Janša, history's first imperial bee teacher.

myths.myth: Slovenia and Slovakia are the same place
myths.fact: They are two entirely separate countries with different languages, histories and locations. Slovakia borders Poland; Slovenia borders Italy and Austria.

myths.myth: Slovenia is Balkan and war-torn like neighbours
myths.fact: Slovenia's 1991 independence war lasted just ten days. It has been a stable EU and NATO member since 2004, among the most prosperous ex-communist states.
